title: Settlement Desk Note — Open-Period Holdback on Ending Net Energy Metering at the Customer's Request
content:
When a customer ends a Net Energy Metering agreement while keeping electric service, part of the most recent export credit is held back for the open billing period when the rate schedule of the Electric Service Agreement hosting the system has on-peak hours.

**Rule.** When the most recent service bill of the hosting service agreement is a summer bill and its schedule has on-peak hours, the holdback share is the summer holdback share of 0.20. When that bill is a winter bill and the schedule has on-peak hours, it is the winter holdback share of 0.10. Otherwise no holdback applies. The open-period holdback is the export credit of the most recent billing period in the net metering history multiplied by the holdback share, rounded to the cent.

**Records read.** The pricing season printed on the most recent service bill of the hosting Electric Service Agreement; whether that agreement's rate schedule has on-peak hours; the export credit with the latest billing period end in the net metering history.

## Holdback share

| Most recent service bill | Hosting schedule | Holdback share |
|---|---|---|
| Summer | Has on-peak hours | 0.20 |
| Winter | Has on-peak hours | 0.10 |
| Summer or winter | No on-peak hours (flat) | None |

## Hypothetical worked cases

Hypothetical input: the most recent export credit in the history is 27.40.

- Summer bill on a time-of-use schedule: 27.40 multiplied by 0.20, a holdback of 5.48.
- Winter bill on a time-of-use schedule: 27.40 multiplied by 0.10, a holdback of 2.74.
- Any bill on a flat schedule: no holdback.
